foreword.text: DEDICATED TO MY PARENTS
This project began in the simplest possible way.
At first, I was only making a list for my own personal use - something that would keep devotional works organised and make them easier for me to find
whenever I needed them.
Then I thought of my mother.
She is deeply religious, so I felt that a well-organised collection of prayers, mantras, hymns and other devotional works could be useful to her as well.
From there, the thought became a little bigger.
If it could help me and help my mother, perhaps it could help the rest of my family too.
Then another thought came to me: why keep it small?
Why not try to make it as complete and useful as possible, so that instead of searching in many different places, a person could find as much as possible in
one place?
And if my family members found it useful and shared it with others, perhaps those people would share it further - and something that began simply for my
own use could slowly reach people I may never even know.
That became the real purpose behind these books.
I especially hope they can help elderly people, children, families, and anyone who wants an easier way to discover or reconnect with their religion &
traditions.
The inspiration to keep improving this work comes greatly from my parents.
From my father, I learned hard work, discipline, perseverance, and the desire to achieve the best possible result. Though religiously inclined, he has always
remained practical and realistic.
From my mother, I learned a more idealistic and deeply devotional way of looking at faith - the belief that prayer, devotion and spirituality can bring
comfort, strength and guidance into everyday life.
Somewhere between my father’s realism and my mother’s faith, this project found its direction.
Today, my hope is simple: that these books are used, shared and passed forward.
From one person to another. From one family to another. From one generation to the next.
And I hope the journey does not end here.
I would like to continue updating these books whenever new and genuine works are discovered, so that they remain living collections rather than finished
volumes.
I also hope, in my spare time, to work towards an application that may one day make these collections even easier to search, explore, listen to and use.
I do not know how far this idea will eventually travel.
But I know where it began -
with a small list made for myself, with the thought that it might help my mother, then my family, and finally, perhaps, many others.
For giving me the values, faith and inspiration from which this journey grew, I dedicate these books, with all my love, respect and gratitude, to my parents.
May something that began within our family eventually reach and help many more.

legend.text: WORK SEARCH
The play icon and complete work title are separate clickable rectangles leading to the same YouTube search-results URL for that individual work.
TIER
Tier displays only T1, T2, T3 or T4. It is an editorial reference classification and is not part of the canonical title.
EVIDENCE-LIMITED FIELDS
A dash in Best Time, Jyotisha or Horoscope Affliction means no sufficiently supported association is asserted.
RECITATION
Preferred Singer / Recitation records a traditional style, lineage or source-backed performer where appropriate.
CANONICAL IDENTITY
Each distinct work receives one hidden permanent CWID. Spelling, script, ordinary translation, performer, recording and routine edition do not create new works.
UNCERTAINTY
Verification may remain probable, disputed, uncertain, unverified, evidence-limited or on hold rather than being forced into certainty.
CROSS-CATEGORY PLACEMENT
The same CWID may appear in more than one category only where each placement is structurally justified.
DEVOTIONAL FORMS
The corpus includes documented mantras, suktas, stotras, namavalis, kavachas, bhajans, kirtans, aartis, abhangs, pasurams, kritis, ritual texts and temple hymns.
TRADITIONAL PURPOSE
Traditional purposes describe attested devotional use and never guarantee an outcome.
DEDICATED SONGS / SCREEN MEDIA
This subsection records source-backed film, television, web-series, theatre or comparable media songs associated with a deity. The media title replaces the
recitation preference; inclusion does not classify the item as canonical liturgy.

rules.text: 42 fixed master categories preserved in their locked numerical order.
One stable hidden CWID represents one genuine work across aliases and justified placements.
No count inflation from spelling, script, translation, performer, recording, publisher or routine edition.
Every deity retains independent identity; small subsections may share a page without canonical merger.
Sacred river deities and Graha deities retain individual subsections within coherent parent groupings.
Work titles use compact typography and exact individual-work YouTube searches.
Blank astrology fields remain dashes unless evidence supports a specific association.
The seven-button footer uses logical page and section navigation.
Index, bookmarks, named destinations and displayed pages derive from the same frozen pagination map.
Maximum defensible coverage is claimed only from accessible and verifiable sources as of the freeze date.
